clue.text: Waterproof articles protecting yellow cloak in the end

indicators.note: the two articles sit either side of the colour, guarding it

parts.note: AN and A are both indefinite articles
OR is gold or yellow in heraldry

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of cloak

parts.note: last letter of cloak

explanation.surface: Someone goes looking for a waterproof coat and settles on a cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: This hooded jacket is a weatherproof outer garment, so the noun 'waterproof' (a raincoat) describes it.

clue.text: Saucy county?

parts.note: an Irish county in the west whose name is also a short informal word for a creamy egg-and-oil sauce

explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' looks like it means cheeky, but it means 'that is a sauce': the county shares its name with the sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: County Mayo in Ireland, and mayo is the casual name for mayonnaise, a dressing.

clue.text: Check viscous fluid including tar, possibly

indicators.note: including means the outer word holds the rearranged letters

parts.note: resin is a sticky, viscous substance from trees

indicators.note: possibly suggests the word tar is one possible arrangement, so it is reshuffled

explanation.surface: A test on some sticky substance that might contain tar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like a noun for an inspection, but it is the verb meaning hold back.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or restrain it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Reptile in bottom of pit turned on Lucifer

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of pit
turned on means sexually aroused, i.e. horny
Lucifer is a name for the devil

explanation.surface: A snake at the bottom of a pit turns on the devil himself.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorny devil is a spiky Australian lizard, so it is an example of a reptile.

clue.text: House gathering later than late in the evening?

indicators.note: later than puts the gathering after the time in the answer

parts.note: at ten (o'clock) is late in the evening
a dance is a social gathering

explanation.surface: A party at someone's house starting at an unusually late hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House gathering' reads as one phrase, but 'House' alone is the definition, in its theatre sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre the house is the audience, and the attendance is the number of people present.

clue.text: Noted art form piercing low area — add sparkle down there?

indicators.note: piercing means the art form goes through the middle of the low area

parts.note: a vale is a valley, a low-lying area
jazz is a musical art form, made of notes

explanation.surface: Piercings and decorations in the nether regions, presented with suggestive innuendo.
explanation.definitionFit: This slang verb means decorating the genital area with crystals or glitter, i.e. adding sparkle in an intimate place.

clue.text: German ship under mass of ice, finally disappearing

indicators.note: in a down clue the ship comes under, i.e. after, the ice
finally disappearing means the last letter of the ice word goes

parts.note: a berg is an iceberg, a floating mass of ice
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A German ship sinks beneath an iceberg, as in a Titanic-style disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A Berliner is a native or resident of Berlin, so a German person.

clue.text: Hollow bit with cutting edges

parts.note: a dent is a hollow
bit as past tense of bite means ate

explanation.surface: A hollow drill bit that has sharp cutting edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentate means toothed or notched, describing a leaf or blade with tooth-like cutting projections.

clue.text: See 4
Exciting soap, perhaps, for best-seller?

parts.note: hot means exciting or sensational
soap often comes as a cake; the 'perhaps' signals an example

explanation.surface: Asking whether a gripping TV soap could become a ratings smash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soap' suggests a TV soap opera, but it is a bar of soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that 'sell like hot cakes' sell fast, so one such item is a popular product.

clue.text: Really short card game ending in walkover for native of New England

indicators.note: short means the word is cut by its final letter

parts.note: very means really
monte is a Spanish gambling card game

indicators.note: ending in points to the last letter of walkover

parts.note: last letter of walkover

explanation.surface: A very brief card game that ends in an easy win for someone from New England.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermont is one of the six New England states, so a person born there is one of its locals.

clue.text: Message from Australia, Melbourne, returned

indicators.note: returned says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A letter sent from Melbourne, Australia, comes back undelivered.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'from' as a link word; it signals that the letters are lifted out of the place names.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic note sent over the internet is a kind of communication or message.

clue.text: Relative keen to cut off cloth

indicators.note: to cut off means the word keen is removed from the cloth

parts.note: nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth
the word keen, taken as written

explanation.surface: A relative who is eager to cut a piece off some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nan is an informal word for a grandmother, a family member.

clue.text: Fancy nuts in fast

parts.note: to fancy something is to like it
nuts means crazy

explanation.surface: Fancy nuts mixed into something during a fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means with great speed or energy, as in 'running flat out'.

clue.text: Narcotics failing to impress a Central American

indicators.note: to impress is to press into, so the A goes inside the shuffled letters
failing suggests the drugs word collapses into a new order

explanation.surface: Drugs that fail to impress someone from Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' rearranges NARCOTICS to COSTRICAN, and 'to impress' presses A into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica lies in Central America, so its citizens are among that region's people.

clue.text: Number are practitioners of meditation?

parts.note: to do something is to practise it
Zen is a school of Buddhism centred on meditation

explanation.surface: Asking how many people practise meditation.
explanation.definitionFit: A twelve, a set quantity, is a number.

clue.text: Member of parliament?

parts.note: the surname of a recent British prime minister and MP, which is also slang for the male member

explanation.walkthrough: The obvious reading is a politician, and that works; the question mark hints at the rude reading of 'member'.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Johnson was an MP, and in slang a johnson is a penis, a bodily member.

clue.text: Meat sauce in that place, right on this spot

parts.note: jus is a thin gravy made from meat juices
there means in that place

explanation.surface: A cook pointing out exactly where the gravy should go.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means precisely here, at this exact position.

clue.text: Nick Henry, winger

parts.note: Hal is a short form of Henry (as Prince Hal, later Henry V)
a finch is a bird, something with wings

explanation.surface: A footballer called Nick Henry who plays on the wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick Henry' reads as a person's name. In Cockney rhyming slang half-inch rhymes with pinch, which means steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Through rhyming slang the phrase means pinch, i.e. steal, which is what nick means in British slang.

clue.text: Company member regrets almost nothing after retirement

indicators.note: retirement means going back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: rues means regrets

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: nada is Spanish-derived slang for nothing

explanation.surface: A retired employee who regrets almost none of their career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' suggests a business, but it is a ballet company; 'retirement' suggests leaving work but means reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A danseur is a male ballet dancer, one of the members of a ballet company.

clue.text: Separate outdoor drier with it, peg out clothes

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the dying word wraps around the rest

parts.note: to peg out is slang for to die

indicators.note: with joins the sun and the word it side by side

parts.note: the sun dries washing hung outdoors

explanation.surface: Instructions for drying laundry: set the outdoor drier going and peg out the clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peg out clothes' looks like hanging washing, but 'peg out' means die and 'clothes' is a verb meaning wraps around.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate is to divide or split apart, the opposite of unite.

clue.text: Saucy dance?

parts.note: a Latin American dance whose name is also that of a spicy tomato sauce

explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' suggests a cheeky dance, but it means a dance that is also a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is both a lively Latin dance and a Mexican-style tomato relish or dip.

clue.text: Outlaw speared criminal, con

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters have gone wrong and are rearranged

parts.note: to do someone is to con or swindle them

explanation.surface: A tale of a bandit who speared someone and cheated a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless, violent criminal, i.e. a lawless bandit.

clue.text: Crack fish found in river

indicators.note: found in means the fish sits inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales/England
cod is a fish

explanation.surface: Someone cracks a fish, as if it were a nut, after finding it in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a code or puzzle is to work it out, i.e. to decipher it.

clue.text: A centre on the other side

parts.note: in football, to centre the ball is to cross it into the middle

explanation.surface: A footballer centres the ball to the far side of the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something over the road is located on the opposite side of it.

clue.text: See 27
Whiskey and port

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a whiskey distilled mainly from this grain
second meaning: a small harbour town in East Sussex, one of the Cinque Ports

explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the fortified wine, a partner for whiskey, but it is a seaport.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye whiskey is a North American spirit, and Rye is an old English coastal town.

clue.text: Island left by territorials touring a country

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the remaining letters surround A
left by means the territorials depart from the island word

parts.note: Tahiti is an island in French Polynesia
TA is the Territorial Army, the British reserve force

explanation.surface: Reservist soldiers leave an island and go on a tour of another country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Island' tempts as the definition, since the answer sits on Hispaniola; the definition is 'country' and the island is one in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti is a Caribbean nation sharing Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic.

clue.text: Another convent resident hit? That's a problem

parts.note: a co-nun is a fellow nun, another resident of the convent
to drum is to beat or hit

explanation.surface: One nun strikes another in the convent, and that causes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum is a puzzling question or difficult dilemma.

clue.text: Yule like Yue, reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly means 'no L' is spoken aloud

parts.note: Yue is Yule with no L, so it is 'no L'

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about whether Yule resembles a word Yue.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the L from Yule and you get Yue; 'no L' said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is another name for Christmas, as is Yule, the midwinter festival.

clue.text: Best-selling author a shade pointless, giant in Croesus?

indicators.note: in puts the other pieces inside the wealthy man

parts.note: Croesus, king of Lydia, was a byword for a rich man

indicators.note: pointless means a compass point letter (N, S, E, W) is removed

parts.note: red is a shade or colour
OS stands for outsize, i.e. giant

explanation.surface: A best-selling writer, a little lacking in point, standing tall among the super-rich.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to Pointless, the BBC quiz show Osman co-hosted, and to his great height; in the wordplay 'pointless' just drops a compass letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Osman's Thursday Murder Club novels have sold millions, making him a hugely successful writer.

clue.text: Central character in custody has justification for crime

indicators.note: central character means the middle letter of the word that follows

parts.note: middle letter of custody
a reason is a justification

explanation.surface: Someone held in custody claims a justification for their crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the offence of betraying one's country, a serious crime.
